title: Key-door maze
summary: Reach the exit on limited energy and time. The key route costs less energy, the detour takes fewer moves, and no single weighting picks between them.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: The smallest maze with a key, a locked door, and a real route choice

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: 14 rooms, 16 one-way passages, and four competing route families

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: 22 rooms, 29 passages, five route families, and cross-route choices

strategies.label: Fewest moves
strategies.description: Breadth-first search: the shortest sequence, whatever it costs.

strategies.label: Least energy
strategies.description: A*, guided by a distance estimate stored in the economy itself.

strategies.label: Pareto: least energy
strategies.description: The lowest-energy point on the exact Pareto frontier, where no route is better on both energy and time.

strategies.label: Pareto: least time
strategies.description: The fastest point on that exact frontier.

title: Sokoban
summary: Push crates onto their goal squares. Every push rewrites three cells at once, and some positions can never be recovered.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Five cells and two pushes

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: A 7×5 board with 35 cells and a ten-step solution

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: An 8×6 board with a longer route and a larger cell economy

strategies.label: Solve puzzle
strategies.description: Breadth-first search over single moves and crate pushes.

title: Exact cover
summary: Choose subsets that cover every element exactly once. A plain search and Algorithm X reach the same answer by different routes.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Four elements and four competing subsets

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Eight elements and twelve subsets arranged as two interacting blocks

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: Twelve elements and eighteen subsets with 27 competing exact covers

strategies.label: Plain search
strategies.description: Breadth-first search with no knowledge of cover structure; it just tries selections.

strategies.label: Algorithm X
strategies.description: Knuth's Algorithm X chooses the moves; the economy still validates every one.

title: Workshop
summary: Build the order from raw stock without creating or destroying material. The fastest plan and the least wasteful plan are not the same plan.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: One chair made from raw stock

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: A six-chair order with competing fast and low-waste recipes

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: A ten-chair order with more material, labor, and production choices

strategies.label: Fewest steps
strategies.description: Breadth-first search: the fewest recipe firings, whatever they waste.

strategies.label: Least waste
strategies.description: Best-first search guided by scrap accumulated in the workshop account.

strategies.label: Pareto: least waste
strategies.description: The lowest-scrap point on the exact Pareto frontier.

strategies.label: Pareto: least time
strategies.description: The fastest point on that exact frontier.

title: Job-shop scheduling
summary: Fit every operation onto a machine without double-booking one or running a job out of order. Finishing one job early delays the other.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Two jobs on the smallest horizon that still forces a machine conflict

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Six ordered operations across three machines and 18 time slots

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: The same operations across a longer eight-slot decision horizon

strategies.label: Shortest makespan
strategies.description: Best-first search on the finish time recorded in the schedule.

strategies.label: Branch optimizer
strategies.description: Depth-first branch-and-bound abandons schedules it can already prove are worse.

strategies.label: Pareto: Job One first
strategies.description: The frontier schedule that finishes Job One earliest.

strategies.label: Pareto: Job Two first
strategies.description: The frontier schedule that finishes Job Two earliest.

title: Uncertain rescue
summary: The survivor's location is unknown. Spend the sensor first, or commit immediately and risk searching the wrong site.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Two possible sites and eight hidden location/sensor outcomes

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Four possible sites, 32 outcomes, an unreliable sensor, and an evacuation leg

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: Six possible sites, 72 outcomes, and at least 256 policy samples

strategies.label: Sense, then move
strategies.description: Spend the sensor, read what Nature reports, then head for the reported site.

strategies.label: Go north immediately
strategies.description: Skip the sensor and commit; the drawn scenario decides whether that pays off.

title: Bridge allocation
summary: One lane, two agents, both need it. Compare first-come priority against an auction that settles bids and access in indivisible steps.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: One crossing round for two agents and one lane

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Two allocation rounds with escrow, recharge, and retained credit

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: Three bounded rounds where priority and spending affect later choices

strategies.label: Plain search
strategies.description: Breadth-first search for any valid crossing order.

strategies.label: First come: A
strategies.description: Agent A gets the first crossing right by arrival order, not by bid.

strategies.label: First come: B
strategies.description: Agent B gets the first crossing right by arrival order, not by bid.

strategies.label: Auction
strategies.description: Bids, winner, escrow, refunds, and crossing rights settle through indivisible changes.

strategies.label: Pareto: favors A
strategies.description: The point on the exact frontier that is best for Agent A.

strategies.label: Pareto: favors B
strategies.description: The point on the exact frontier that is best for Agent B.

title: Multi-party marketplace
summary: Settle orders across buyers, sellers, carriers, the platform, and tax in one indivisible step. When it fails, you see exactly which account fell short and by how much.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Two orders across three buyers, three sellers, and one active carrier

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Four linked orders across 14 accounts sharing budget, stock, shipping capacity, and tax

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: Six linked orders across 16 accounts with exactly enough stock and shipping capacity

strategies.label: Clear the market
strategies.description: Pick orders that can all settle together without overdrawing any account.

strategies.label: Pareto: favors buyers
strategies.description: The clearing on the exact frontier with the highest total buyer benefit.

strategies.label: Pareto: favors sellers
strategies.description: The clearing on the exact frontier with the highest total seller benefit.

title: Stochastic logistics
summary: Deliver four orders through weather and breakdowns. The short route wins when nothing goes wrong; the long one finishes more often when things do.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Two deliveries with a compact route and a small sample budget

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Four deliveries with recurring weather and breakdowns

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: The four-delivery network evaluated with at least 256 stochastic rollouts

strategies.label: Direct route
strategies.description: The shortest route, fastest when weather and breakdowns cooperate.

strategies.label: Reliable route
strategies.description: A longer route that completes more often when they do not.

strategies.label: MCTS
strategies.description: Monte Carlo tree search plans the next move by sampling how chance could unfold.

title: Connect Four
summary: A full game of Connect Four played by MCTS on both sides, with gravity and every winning line written as rules.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: A compact board with a short game and few rollouts

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: The full 7×6 board and all 69 winning lines

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: The full board with four times the MCTS work per move

strategies.label: MCTS self-play
strategies.description: Monte Carlo tree search plays both colours until someone wins or the board fills.

title: Hidden-information mission
summary: Two agents each see only part of the map. Compare sharing what they see before acting against both moving straight in.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: Two hidden scenarios and one private sighting

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Sixteen hidden scenarios with private sightings, belief updates, and hazards

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: The same mission evaluated with at least 256 belief-conditioned simulations

strategies.label: Scout, share, then move
strategies.description: One agent looks, tells the other, and both act on the updated picture.

strategies.label: Both go north
strategies.description: Neither agent looks or shares; replay keeps whatever goes wrong.

title: Perishable inventory
summary: Ten thousand units spoil by batch, not one at a time. Cooling costs energy, and a power outage forces the tradeoff.

instances.label: Micro
instances.description: One hundred units split between two batches

instances.label: Showcase
instances.description: Ten thousand units with cooling, deadlines, and a power outage

instances.label: Stress
instances.description: One million units using the same two batch-level condition facts

strategies.label: Power outage
strategies.description: Refrigeration fails, and every batch past its deadline spoils at once.

strategies.label: Pareto: save stock
strategies.description: The storage plan on the exact frontier that keeps the most usable units.

strategies.label: Pareto: save energy
strategies.description: The storage plan that spends the least cooling energy.
